sec: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS features and medical therapy · p848

items.q: On inferior petrosal sinus sampling, a petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio above what value is significant for a pituitary adenoma?
items.exp: Petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio >2:1 (significant) → pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy; <2 → PET scan → PNS. (Book p848)

items.q: A petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio <2 directs the work-up to:
opts: PET scan and a diagnosis of paraneoplastic syndrome
items.exp: <2 ratio → PET scan → Dx PNS (paraneoplastic syndrome). (Book p848)

items.q: The high-dose DST regimen and its positive result are:
opts: 2 mg Q6H × 2 days; >50% suppression = pituitary cause
items.exp: High-dose DST 2 mg Q6H × 2d with >50% suppression indicates a pituitary cause. (Book p848)

items.q: The clinical features of paraneoplastic (ectopic ACTH) syndrome include:
opts: Hyperpigmentation, less protein catabolism, and mineralocorticoid action (HTN, mA, hypokalaemia)
items.exp: PNS: hyperpigmentation, less protein catabolism, mineralocorticoid action — HTN, mA, hypokalaemia. (Book p848)

items.q: The treatment of choice for Cushing's disease (and relapse-fit patients) is:
items.exp: Trans-sphenoidal surgery is TOC with a 75% remission rate; radiotherapy is 3rd line if unfit for surgery. (Book p848)

items.q: The remission rate after trans-sphenoidal surgery is:
items.exp: 75% remission rate after trans-sphenoidal surgery. (Book p848)

items.q: Match the medical therapy — 1) Glucocorticoid receptor inhibitor  2) Adrenolytic in adrenal cancer  3) Prevents relapse (listed first) … A) Mifepristone  B) Mitotane  C) Ketoconazole
items.exp: Mifepristone = glucocorticoid receptor inhibitor; mitotane = adrenolytic in adrenal cancer; ketoconazole (with pasireotide, cabergoline, metyrapone) prevents relapse. (Book p848)

items.q: For patients unfit for surgery, the third-line option is:
items.exp: If not fit for surgery → radiotherapy (3rd line). (Book p848)

items.q: Which drug is NOT listed among the relapse-preventing medical therapies?
items.exp: Listed: ketoconazole, pasireotide, cabergoline, metyrapone (II doc), mifepristone, mitotane — not spironolactone. (Book p848)
